sentences.text: Shri R.P. Gupta- learned counsel for the appellant/claimants.

Shri Nirendra Singh Tomar, learned counsel for the respondent 
 Company.

Order 
This appeal by the appellant/claimant u/S. 173 (1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 is arising out of the award dated 22.02.2013 passed by Third MACT, District- Shivpuri (in short "Claims Tribunal")
in Claim Case No.155/2011 on account of exonerating insurance company from the liability.
2.The date of accident and negligence are not in dispute and the findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal in this regard are not in question.

3. As per findings of the Claims Tribunal, for the case of death of Ratanlal, an amount of compensation to the tune of Rs.4,41,500/- has been awarded by the Claims Tribunal with interest from filing of claim petition till its realization.
4. Learned counsel for the appellant filed this appeal on the ground that the trial Court found the breach of policy condition.

It is true that at the time of the accident owner and driver have no permit of the offending vehicle but tribunal committed error in totally exonerating insurance company from payment of compensation.
Therefore, NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:17112 2 MA-449-2013 prays for setting aside the finding regarding exoneration of Insurance company from payment of compensation.

sentences.text: 5. On the other hand learned counsel of Insurance Company supported the impugned award and pray for rejection of appeal.

6. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
7.
After hearing learned counsel of both the parties, it is found that at the time of accident owner of the offending vehicle has no permit.
It is breach of the policy.
It is also undisputed that deceased was third party.

In the light of judgement in the case o f Amrit Paul Singh vs. TATA AIG, General Insurance Company Ltd. reported in 2019 (2) MPLJ (SC) 8, the Apex Court held that Insurance Company shall be liable to make payment of the compensation with liberty to recover the same from the owner.

entities.text: Amrit Paul Singh vs. TATA AIG, General Insurance Company Ltd. reported in 2019 (2) MPLJ (SC) 8
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 8. In view of the aforesaid discussion, the appeal is partly allowed to the extent that Insurance Company shall pay the compensation to the claimants but the Insurance Company shall be at liberty to recover from the owner of the offending vehicle as per "pay and recover policy".
9. Accordingly, the appeal is partly allowed to the extent indicated above.
